title: FII Tax Exemption on G-Secs: What Changed and Why it Matters
description: The Indian government has exempted Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) from taxes on interest income and capital gains derived from Indian Government Secur.

faq.a: A G-Sec, or Government Security, is a tradable instrument issued by the Central or State Governments to borrow money. These are considered highly safe as they carry practically no risk of default.

faq.q: Who benefits from this tax exemption?
faq.a: The primary beneficiaries are Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) or Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) who invest in Indian Government Securities.

faq.q: Does this exemption apply to all types of Indian bonds?
faq.a: No, this exemption specifically applies to Indian Government Securities (G-Secs), which include central government dated securities and treasury bills, as notified by the government.

faq.q: Will this affect my personal investments in debt mutual funds?
faq.a: While the exemption directly benefits FIIs, increased foreign investment in G-Secs could indirectly lead to lower bond yields in India, potentially impacting the returns of debt mutual funds that hold these securities.

faq.q: What is the main objective behind this tax exemption?
faq.a: The main objectives are to attract more foreign capital into India's bond market, help stabilise the Indian Rupee, and deepen the overall debt market.

faq.q: When did this tax exemption come into effect?
faq.a: The effective date of the exemption is specified in the official notification issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).
